title: A remote outpost of the Milky Way
caption: The globular cluster NGC 7006, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 7006 · constellation Delphinus · about 140000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image shows NGC 7006, a compact and distant globular cluster in Delphinus, the Dolphin, among the tiniest of the constellations. Because it is modest in size, very far away and relatively faint, amateur astronomers often overlook it, yet Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys renders it bright and clear.

NGC 7006 lies in the outskirts of the Milky Way, about 135 000 light-years away, or five times as far as the Sun is from the galactic centre. It belongs to the galactic halo, a roughly spherical zone of dark matter, gas and thinly spread star clusters. Its highly eccentric orbit hints that it may have been born on its own, inside a small outside galaxy that the Milky Way then captured.

Distant as it is, the cluster is far nearer than the numerous faint background galaxies in the frame. Each of those faint smudges probably has its own family of globular clusters like NGC 7006, too faint for even Hubble to see.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.21 x 3.21 arcminutes) and distance (140000 light years), the frame spans roughly 131 × 131 light-years. Its light set out about 140,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, combining visible and near-infrared light. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and this cluster is too faint and small for most amateur telescopes to show in such detail.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Remote clusters like this one offer important clues to how stars formed and gathered in the Milky Way's halo. The image combines visible and near-infrared light and covers a field a little over 3 by 3 arcminutes.
alt: A compact globular cluster with many faint galaxies in the background.
